tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Artaud and Theatre of Cruelty

questions.question: Explain what Artaud meant by 'Theatre of Cruelty' — why is 'cruelty' misleading?
questions.correctAnswer: 'Cruelty' means intensity and rigour, not physical pain. Artaud wanted theatre to be a shock to the system that awakens the audience's subconscious — an assault on the senses that strips away rational civilised responses.

questions.question: How would you use Artaud's ideas to create a sensory, immersive experience for an audience?
questions.correctAnswer: Practical examples: surround-sound audience, performers among spectators, harsh lighting changes, drumming rhythms, exaggerated physical gesture, symbolic objects, no conventional set. Each choice linked to Artaud's theory.

questions.question: Compare Artaud's approach to theatre with Brecht's. How do they want the audience to respond differently?
questions.correctAnswer: Brecht wants the audience to THINK critically (V-effect, alienation); Artaud wants the audience to FEEL viscerally (immersion, sensory assault). Brecht distances; Artaud overwhelms. Both reject naturalism but for opposite reasons.
